{{Hatnote|For the product, see [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]].}}
'''Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck''' is a Star Wars CCG sealed-deck format in which each player opens one [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] box. [[Decipher]] first ran it at [[DecipherCon 2000]] in October 2000, before the product reached stores, and gave it its own ability rule in November 2000.<ref name="dcon-sw-events">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/starwarsccg.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game events], DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010126213800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/starwarsccg.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="fkl2">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="jpsdrule">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/jpsdruleschange.html New Official Rule for Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck Environment], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010124153500/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/resources/jpsdruleschange.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== Card pool ==
"Each player will receive one Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck box to wage a battle on Tatooine."<ref name="dcon-sw-events" /> At the first event the box held "twenty exclusive premium cards and six Jabba's Palace expansion packs", players built 40-card decks, and games had a 40-minute limit.<ref name="fkl2" /> The Light Side premiums were ten cards, among them the objective [[Agents In The Court / No Love For The Empire]] and [[Lando With Vibro-Ax]].<ref name="jpsd-ls">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/jabbaspalacesealeddeck/light/index.html Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck Light Side Card List], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001017142720/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/jabbaspalacesealeddeck/light/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Ability rule ===
On 10 November 2000 Decipher added a rule for this format only:<ref name="jpsdrule" />
: "Any character of ability 1 who has an unmodified (printed on the card) deploy number of 3 or greater is considered, for all purposes, to be of ability 2. (This rule applies to both Dark Side and Light Side characters)"
Decipher called it "an officially sanctioned tournament rule for the JPSD Sealed Deck tournament environment", meant "to balance gameplay within the JPSD environment". It "does not apply to tournaments using Standard Constructed Deck rules, or to any other Closed Environment or Sealed Deck environment." Tournament directors were to use it from the weekend of 10 November 2000.<ref name="jpsdrule" /> Decipher's 2001 tournament resources linked the same notice as the "Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck Format".<ref name="res-sw" />

=== GEMP ===

== History ==
DecipherCon 2000 scheduled five Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck events, all sanctioned, four games, entry $20: Thursday 5 October at noon (#SW211) and 9 p.m. (#SW214), Friday 6 October at 6 p.m. (#SW223), and Saturday 7 October at 10 a.m. (#SW231) and 6 p.m. (#SW234). "Here's your chance to play with these cards weeks before your friend's back home will get a chance to play with them."<ref name="dcon-sw-events" /><ref name="dcon00-sched">[http://www2.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swccgevents.pdf DecipherCon Master Tournament Schedule for Decipher Games], DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030413152501/http://www2.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swccgevents.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

Francis K. Lalumiere reported the first event, on the morning of 5 October 2000: 24 players in a side hall while Day 1 of the World Championship ran in the main hall. The Light Side dominated; [[Koen Meijssen]] (8, +69) beat [[Martin Akesson]] (6, +17) by 3 Force in the final confrontation. Jeff Weitkamp (Gold 40) was tournament director.<ref name="fkl2" />

The Players Committee's Alternate Format Tournament Guide has a draft version, "JPOTSD Booster Draft": one Jabba's Palace Official Tournament Sealed Deck per player, the same ability rule, the premium packs opened as in sealed play and only the booster packs drafted. Its "Secret Squirrel" format also uses this product.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>
